title: From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay with the National Minimum Wage and the Adecco Salary Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Compare the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and the Adecco salary guide for market benchmarks.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour yields an annual gross of $52,257.44, with super and tax estimated separately.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour equals $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,257.44 per year.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). When using our timesheet calculator, you can check the casual loading box to add this automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator adds it for you.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my annual pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage, super would be $52,257.44 × 12% = $6,270.89, added to your total remuneration. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution by your employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you receive an hourly rate or a salary offer, knowing how it translates to annual pay is essential for budgeting, comparing jobs, and understanding your entitlements. The standard approach in Australia is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time roles, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Act.

This article explains the conversion process, highlights the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates, and shows how the **Adecco salary** guide can provide market context without overriding legal minimums.

## The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most Australian workers are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates for specific industries and occupations. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database provides detailed classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

For example, a retail employee may have a base rate above $26.44, plus weekend penalties. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides list the minimum pay rates for each award, including full-time, part-time, and casual classifications. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate – for the National Minimum Wage, that’s $33.05 per hour.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual

The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. We use 38 hours as the standard full-time week. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust accordingly.

**Example using the National Minimum Wage:**
- Hourly: $26.44
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (close to the official $1,004.90 (rounding difference due to rounding))
- Fortnightly: $2,009.44
- Annual: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,257.44

This is your gross annual pay. On top of this, your employer must pay superannuation at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. For this example, super adds $6,270.89.

### Tax and Medicare

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates (from the Australian Taxation Office):
- Tax-free threshold: $0–$18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For $52,257.44, tax would be approximately $6,702 (calculated as $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 = $4,020, plus 30% on $7,257.44 = $2,177.23, total $6,197.23, plus Medicare 2% = $1,045.15, total around $7,242). This is an estimate; use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise figure.

## Using the Adecco Salary Guide

The **Adecco salary** guide offers a broad overview of market salaries across industries like accounting, IT, and trades. It is useful for negotiation and understanding typical pay ranges, but it is not a substitute for award rates or the National Minimum Wage. For example, the guide may suggest a higher range for a role, but your legal minimum is still the award rate. Always check the relevant award via the [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Commission database.

## Practical Considerations

- **Casual loading**: If you are casual, remember the 25% loading is added to the base rate. Our [timesheet](/) calculator includes a checkbox for this – never enter a rate that already includes loading.
- **Overtime and penalties**: The conversion assumes the same rate every week. Real pay may include overtime, penalty rates, and allowances – these are not in this basic conversion.
- **Super is on top**: Super is 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings, not deducted from your salary.
- **Salary packaging and packaging can affect tax, but are not included here.

For a full picture, see the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) topics.

## Conclusion

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by 38 hours and 52 weeks. The National Minimum Wage sets the floor, awards set higher minimums, and the **Adecco salary** guide provides market context. Always verify your specific award rate using official sources. Use our calculator to estimate your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, including casual loading and super.
